title: Alex's editor
body: Alex writes code in Neovim with a deliberately minimal setup: LSP, treesitter, fzf, and nothing else. Plugin soup is explicitly unwelcome.

title: Alex's caffeine rules
body: Alex drinks one espresso on waking and switches to water for the rest of the day. Anything caffeinated after noon wrecks Alex's sleep.

title: Alex's timezone
body: Alex lives in Austin, Texas — US Central time (UTC-6, UTC-5 during daylight saving). Schedule everything with that offset in mind.

title: Focus music
body: For deep-focus work Alex plays instrumental music only — ambient, film scores, modular synth sets. Anything with lyrics breaks concentration.

title: Alex's dietary constraints
body: Alex is vegetarian and has a peanut allergy. Restaurant and recipe suggestions must satisfy both constraints.

title: Alex's peak hours
body: Alex does the deepest thinking in the morning, roughly 9 to noon, and guards that window from meetings.

title: Alex's reading habits
body: Alex reads science fiction before bed; the current rotation is Iain M. Banks, Adrian Tchaikovsky, and Ursula K. Le Guin.

title: License preference
body: Personal projects ship under the MIT license unless a dependency's license forces something else.

title: SearXNG endpoint
body: Dream's web searches go through a local SearXNG metasearch instance listening on 127.0.0.1:8888 — never a hosted search API.

title: Dream state layout
body: Dream keeps runtime state in data/dream.db (SQLite in WAL mode) and mirrors long-term memories to human-editable markdown under memory/.

title: MachX inference server
body: MachX is the local OpenAI-compatible inference server used for offline work; it currently serves Qwen2.5-3B.

title: Camoufox browsing
body: Web pages are fetched with Camoufox, a hardened stealth Firefox build that renders JavaScript-heavy and bot-protected pages where a plain HTTP fetch fails.

title: Embedding model
body: Semantic recall runs on fastembed with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 — 384-dimensional normalized vectors, CPU-only inference.

title: Espresso gear
body: The espresso machine is a Gaggia Classic Pro with the 9-bar OPV spring mod and a bottomless portafilter.

title: Home network map
body: Home network: UniFi gateway at 192.168.1.1, NAS at 192.168.1.20, and the server rack on the 192.168.1.32/28 subnet.

title: Project Aurora
body: Project Aurora is the codename for the personal-finance dashboard rebuild. Stack: SvelteKit front end, FastAPI back end, Postgres. Key decision on auth lives in [[aurora-auth-decision]].

title: Aurora auth decision
body: Auth will be passkeys only — no passwords at all. Decided after the March security review flagged credential reuse as the top risk.

title: Shipping a release
body: To ship a release: run the full test suite, bump the version in pyproject.toml, tag vX.Y.Z, push the tag, and let CI build the wheel. Never tag from a dirty tree.

title: Debugging a misbehaving tool
body: When a Dream tool misbehaves: check var/logs/ first, then rerun with DREAM_PERMISSION_MODE=default to surface raw permission prompts, then bisect with the tool's own test.

title: Deep work blocks
body: Deep work protocol: 90-minute blocks, notifications off, phone in another room, exactly one written goal per block, five-minute walk between blocks.

title: Backup routine
body: Backups: data/ and memory/ rsync nightly to the NAS. Before pruning old snapshots, verify the checksum manifest matches; a backup that isn't verified doesn't exist.

title: Workstation GPU notes
body: The workstation build prioritizes silence over raw airflow, which has a few consequences worth remembering. The case is a Fractal Torrent with the stock 180mm intakes swapped to run at fixed low RPM, and the whole machine sits inside the closed left cabinet of the desk, which adds roughly four to six degrees to every component under sustained load compared to open-air. The AIO for the CPU exhausts out the top, and its fan curve is tied to coolant temperature rather than core temperature, so short bursty loads stay whisper quiet while long renders slowly ramp the fans over about ten minutes. The NVMe drives run hot in summer because they sit under the GPU backplate; the fix that worked was a cheap finned heatsink on the primary drive plus removing the decorative shroud. Now the part that actually matters for performance: the RTX 4090 will thermal-throttle inside that cabinet during summer afternoons unless its power limit is capped — run nvidia-smi -pl 350 to hold it at 350 watts, which costs about four percent performance and completely eliminates the throttling and the fan surging that comes with it. A udev rule applies the cap at boot, so if the card is ever mysteriously slow after a driver update, check that the rule survived before debugging anything else. Dust filters get vacuumed on the first of the month; the intake filter clogs noticeably faster in spring.

title: 2026-05-12: server moved to rack
body: Moved the home server out of the closet into the rack. New address 192.168.1.40. About two hours of downtime; DNS was the only casualty.

title: 2026-06-03: Aurora kickoff
body: Kicked off the Project Aurora rebuild. Agreed on SvelteKit plus FastAPI, first milestone end of June: read-only dashboard against real transaction data.

title: 2026-06-20: GPU upgrade
body: Installed the RTX 4090 in the workstation and moved the old 3080 into the server for inference duty. Had to cap the 4090's power limit for thermals — see the workstation GPU notes.

title: 2026-07-01: Dream gained vision
body: Dream gained vision: the new see tool reads screenshots from the browser and arbitrary local images. First real use was reading a chart off a dashboard screenshot.
